_comment: Constitutional PreToolUse gate — merge this `hooks` block into your .claude/settings.json.
It is shipped as an EXAMPLE rather than applied, for two reasons. First, .claude/settings.json
is gitignored in this repository, so a block written there reaches one machine and no other —
the hook script itself is tracked, but its wiring cannot be. Second, agentteams never writes a
user's settings.json directly (see agentteams/hooks_emit.py): clobbering operator config is a
worse failure than an unwired hook.
Without this block the hook is inert, and C-5 has no reach over agent tool calls — which is
exactly the gap probe E3 measured. Wiring it is a deliberate operator action.
What it does: denies a Write/Edit whose content the scanner rates high severity (credentials,
PII paths, injected override text), and asks before a Bash command matching a Mandatory Review
Trigger (sudo, pipe-to-shell, recursive delete, persistence, package install, forced push).
To remove it: delete the `hooks` key.

Invoked through `python3` rather than as a bare path: the generation pipeline writes files with the umask default (0644) and never sets an executable bit, so a bare-path command would land a hook that LOOKS installed and silently fails with 'permission denied'. Found by rehearsing a fleet update against an isolated copy. Interpreter invocation also survives clone, copy and archive extraction, which an exec bit does not.
